question: Why should the fire of dissolution abandon its fierce display and become calm within itself?
premises: The cosmic fire is addressed as blazing with ostentatious flames and sparks.
There is nothing left for it to burn.
The universe has already been pervaded and dissolved into what is essentially its own light.
inference: Therefore the fire of dissolution should withdraw its fierce display and rest calmly in itself.
plain_english: Grow calm of yourself within the self; quickly abandon your ostentatious display of flaming matted locks, O fire of cosmic dissolution. There is nothing left for you to burn now, because by hundreds of terrible, dense, whirling sparks of your blazing, this universe has been pervaded and swiftly dissolved, becoming of the nature of your own light.
